subject: Missing valid days in section 4 and 5 output

messages.author: 620c75bd616edf6f
messages.subject: Missing valid days in section 4 and 5 output
parts:
Hi All,

 

I’m using GGIR to process my 7-day actigraph data. I’m getting fewer days of output data in section 4 and 5 compared to section 2. The full 7 days appear in section 2, but only 3 or 4 appear in section 4 and 5. Section 4 and 5 often starts with the day we posted the acti to the participant, has a few missing days when it was in transit then ends at day 7 missing the valid data beyond day 7. I want it to start on the day the participant starts wearing it (usually around day 4) and go for 7 days from that point.

 

My script is pasted below and milestone data from an example participant can be found here https://www.dropbox.com/s/8zi0lxmh81elvr3/meta_200_ID.RAW.csv.RData?dl=0.

 

I’ve also tried strategy 2 and 3, editing hrs.del.start depending on when participants started wearing their acti, changing section 5 to be from midnight to midnight (MM) in line with section 2, setting exclude first last day to true and reducing includenight/daycrit.

 

Any thoughts on what I’m doing wrong? I’m out of ideas of what to try.

 

Thanks for your time!

Steph

 

library(GGIR)

g.shell.GGIR(

  #-------------------------------

  # General parameters

  #-------------------------------

  mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),

  datadir="//myinputdir/",

  outputdir="//myoutputdir/",

  studyname = "A4L_data",

  overwrite = TRUE,

  do.imp=TRUE,

  idloc=2,

  print.filename=TRUE,

  #-------------------------------

  # Part 1 parameters:

  #-------------------------------

  windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),

  do.cal=TRUE,

  do.enmo = TRUE,

  do.anglez=TRUE,

  chunksize=1,

  printsummary=TRUE,

  desiredtz="Australia/Queensland",

  #-------------------------------

  # Part 2 parameters:

  #-------------------------------

  strategy = 1,

  ndayswindow=7,

  hrs.del.start = 0,

  hrs.del.end = 0,

  maxdur = 14,

  includedaycrit = 4,

  M5L5res = 10,

  winhr = c(5,10),

  qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),

  qwindow =c(0,24),

  mvpathreshold =c(100),

  ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),

  bout.metric = 4,

  closedbout=FALSE,

 

  #-------------------------------

  # Part 3 parameters:

  #-------------------------------

  Timethreshold = c(5),

  Anglethreshold =5,

  ignorenonwear = TRUE,

  #-------------------------------

  # Part 4 parameters:

  #-------------------------------

  excludefirstlast = FALSE,

  includenightcrit = 4,

  relyonsleeplog=TRUE,

  loglocation= "//myloglocation/",

  do.visual = TRUE,

  outliers.only = FALSE,

  criterror = 4,

  sleeplogidnum = TRUE,

  colid=1,

  coln1=2,

  nnights = 7,

  #-------------------------------

  # Part 5 parameters:

  #-------------------------------

  threshold.lig = c(40),

  threshold.mod = c(100),

  threshold.vig = c(400),

  Excludefirstlast.part5 = FALSE,

  boutcriter = 0.8,

  boutcriter.in = 0.9,

  boutcriter.lig = 0.8,

  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,

  boutdur.in = c(10,20,30),

  boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10),

  boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),

  timewindow = c("WW"),

  #-----------------------------------

  # Report generation

  #-------------------------------

  do.report=c(2,4,5),

  visualreport=TRUE,    

  dofirstpage = TRUE,

  viewingwindow=1)

parts:
Hi Vincent.

 

I really appreciate you getting back to me. I have thoroughly checked the previous question you referred to as well as other similar discussions, however I believe my issue is different. I have updated my GGIR to 1.10-7, specified exclude firstlast = FALSE, however I am still seeing missing days in part 4 and 5 output. It is not that I am just missing a few of the first and last days, I am often missing 6 out of 7 or completely different days are shown in part 4 and 5 compared to part 2. 


Part 4 and 5 often starts with the days that the acti is turned on and/or posted rather than the days the participant wears the acti, then stops at day 7 from that point. These incorrect start dates also results in the sleep log dates being completely mismatched to the Actidata (i.e sleep log day 1 is matched to the day the acti is turned on, not when the participant starts wearing it 5 or so days later). Any thoughts on anything I could try?  

 

Thanks so much for your time,

Steph

Hi Vincent,

 

Thanks so much for checking in. I am still having the issue with GGIR version 1.11-0. I’ve worked out if I match my sleep log start date to the day they actually started wearing their acti (as the system auto matches it to the day it was turned on), I’m getting fewer missing days. However, I am still seeing 2 – 4 missing days in part 5 (usually the last days) even though part 2 indicated over 16 hours (usually 24 hours) valid wear time on those days. I've attached the output from an example file. I'm not sure what else to try. 


Many thanks,

Steph
